inputs.original_text: You won't believe how Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week trying to spin that housing tenancies have gone up, but the real issue is the rise in eviction notices and homelessness that followed the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Nationally, the number of people stuck in emergency accommodation has increased again, which just goes to show how these weak measures fail to protect vulnerable groups from the structural inequalities and landlord power that drive the housing crisis. We urgently need serious reforms to tackle the root causes of exploitation and secure stable homes as a basic right rather than letting profits come first—it's time the system stopped serving the powerful at the expense of everyone else.
inputs.modified_text: Micheál Martin was in Limerick this past week trying to spin that housing tenancies have gone up, but the real damage comes from the government's March 1 rules forcing landlords to offer six-year leases. Those heavy-handed mandates have triggered a clear rise in eviction notices and homelessness, and nationally the number of people in emergency accommodation has increased again. This is what happens when politicians override private agreements and property rights with top-down controls that drive landlords out of the market entirely. It undermines family stability and social order by reducing available homes instead of letting responsible owners and tenants work things out. These progressive interventions never deliver and only make the housing mess worse for ordinary people who value self-reliance over endless government fixes.
